newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 15.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Pioneer
BOFORS DEALS MADE VIA PM'S OFFICE, CBI REPORT ALLEGES

The Central Bureau of Investigation's report on the Bofors case, already submitted to the government, confirmed the close links between former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi and Italian busiessman Ottavio Quattrocchi. Without naming Gandhi as an accused, the report said Quattrocchi had direct access to the former prime minister and his office. The Special Investigative Team's report also detailed Quattrocchi's political influence which helped him to get a large number of contracts besides the defence deal.
The Times Of India
PARLIAMENT CRITICISES INVESTIGATING AGENCY

The lower house of parliament criticised the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) for making selective leaks to the media on sensitive matters like the Bofors probe without taking parliament into confidence. A Congress party member criticised the CBI chief's action of not informing parliament about the agency's reported decision to charge former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi. The proposition for granting autonomy to investigating and enforcement agencies was also opposed by the members.
The Observer
LEFT PARTIES SOUR OVER GOVERNMENT ECONOMIC POLICY

The left parties said the financial policy of the government marked a gross deviation from the common minimum programme (CMP) and decided to raise the issue at the coming steering committee meeting. The Left Front felt the financial policy had been conveniently selective in implementing the CMP, completely disregarding its letter and spirit. The Communist Party of India-Marxist accused the financial policy of betraying its class bias on the move to cut subsidies across the board, which the party said would mean the reduction of the meagre facilities being given to the people, thus worsening their economic miseries.
The Economic Times
STATE TRADING CORP TO PROFIT THROUGH RECAST

The State Trading Corporation (STC) embarked on a restructuring exercise which might take its turnover to around 30 billion rupees in 1997/98 (April-March). It had decided to organise itself into different profit centres, set up a manufacturing base for several products, create branded products, and enter the domestic market in a major way to cross-subsidise any losses incurred in the export market.
GLOBALSTAR GETS SPECIAL CASE CLEARANCE

Foreign investment in Globalstar India Satellite Service for its international hand-held telephone project has been cleared. The defence ministry cleared the proposal as a special case allowing the company to undertake only preliminary technical surveys at the moment. However, the ministry decided not to clear any such proposals in the future. A similar project of Afro-Asian Satellite Communications and Mobile Communications Holding was earlier rejected as the department of space and the ministry of defence expressed their reservations on the proposal.
GE CAPITAL TO SET NEW BENCHMARK FOR BORROWINGS

GE Capital Services was poised to set a new benchmark for borrowings by finance companies by placing an 18-month paper at a coupon of 13.25 percent. This would be significantly lower than what it had paid on its earlier borrowings. The paper formed a part of the entire yield curve, from 18 months to 60 months, that GE Capital was offering institutional investors for the very first time on its latest 800 million rupee bond issue. Its earlier offerings comprised paper of varying tenor, but issued at different times, and at much higher interest rates.
RBI REVIEWS EARLIER DIRECTIVE

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is re-examining its earlier directive asking banks to credit any excess depreciation provisioning in investments to the profit and loss account. RBI sources said the re-examination was prompted by the realisation that if banks followed RBI's directives, it would end up inflating the net profit for 1996/97 (April-March).
BAN ON AZO DYES FROM JUNE 23

A environment ministry notification has banned the use of azo dyes, widely used in the textile industry, from June 23. The ban would apply to the entire country and include all substances containing about 70 azo dyes specified in the notification. A draft notification proposing the ban was issued on March 29, 1996. It invoked objections and suggestions from the public as well as the concerned parties. The government duly considered these representations before imposing the ban.
FULL INSURANCE TO LARGE COMPANIES

The Tariff Advisory Committee has finally cleared the General Insurance Corporation's (GIC) proposal to issue a blanket industrial risks policy to large firms. Following the clearance, this policy could now be issued by the four GIC subsidiaries. The policy would enable corporates to obtain cover for all their property from any kind of physical loss or damage under a single document. The cover would be available to companies with a minimum sum insured of one billion rupees.
Financial Express
LIQUID FUEL ALLOTMENT TO BE WITHIN ALLOWED LIMIT

The Petroleum Ministry has told the Power Ministry that the liquid fuel allotment should be within the sanctioned limit of 12,000 megawatts. This ended weeks of inter-ministerial haggling and manoeuvres by state governments and interest groups. Roughly 1.25 million tonnes of naphtha would be required to generate 1000 megawatts of electricity. A ministry official said naphtha was not a preferred fuel and added that the country was poised to become deficient in the expensive light refinery distillate by next year.
INDUSTRIAL BANK TO RAISE TERM DEPOSITS

The Industrial Development Bank (IDBI) has taken the lead in floating one-year term deposits following the RBI's decision to allow financial institutions to raise short-term resources. IDBI would be offering 11 percent interest on one-year fixed deposits. It might change the rates later in accordance with responses. IDBI pegged the interest rate for two-year deposits at 12 percent and three-year deposits at 12.5 percent.
Business Standard
BOMBAY BOURSE LINES UP MAJOR STOCKS RESHUFFLE

In a major restructuring, the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) is conducting the first-ever review of over 6,000 stocks listed at the exchange. The BSE plans to expand B1 group stocks, while trimming the B2 group by month end. The exchange also wants to enlarge the A group, which now contains about 80 stocks, by adding some from the B1 group. According to top exchange officials, the B1 group would be increased from the existing 700 to over 1,000 stocks.
BAJAJ AUTO NET UP TO 4.4 BLN RUPEES

Bajaj Auto's growth in sales and profit dipped in 1996/97 (April-March) along with its share of the two and three wheeler market. During the year, sluggish for the auto industry, the sales of the country's largest two and three wheeler maker grew 16.1 percent to 32.44 billion rupees, while net profit rose 5.4 percent to 4.4 billion rupees from 4.18 billion rupees in the previous year. In 1995/96, sales had grown 28 percent and net profit 36 percent over 1994/95.
TEMPORARY BAN ON FOREIGN INVESTMENT IN BROADCASTING

All foreign direct investment (FDI) proposals in the information and broadcasting sector are banned until a comprehensive broadcasting law is in place. This implies that FDI proposals worth millions of dollars, including expansion plans of Sony Entertainment Television and STAR TV, as well as fresh proposals to enter the electronic media, will be held up.
The Observer
GOVERNMENT OFFERS TO BUY SUZUKI STAKE IN MARUTI

The government has offered to buy out Suzuki Motor's 50 percent stake in Maruti Udyog Ltd (MUL), the bluechip car joint venture. This followed an offer to this effect made by Suzuki to the industry minister some time ago. Suzuki had suggested that either one of the partners buy out a part of the other's equity in the company to enable one of them to get absolute management control in the company. The government's latest move was in response to Suzuki's recent missive demanding all expansion plans in MUL be put on hold till the issues relating to equity and investment were settled.
NO HASTE IN REMOVING CONTROLS ON IMPORTS

India would not take any hasty decision on the removal of quantitative restrictions on its imports, the commerce secretary said. He said although India's balance of payments position had improved, her forex inflows continued to be volatile. New Delhi sought the European Union's support for a systematic approach and indicated its willingness to hold further discussions with the group. The European delegation expressed hope that India would phase out all quantitative restrictions within two years to conform with trade-related intellectual property rights agreements.
